data.title: Charging Dock Replacement
data.description:
The most common issues with the iPhone 16 Pro charging dock are:

  • The battery charges very slowly
  • iPhone 16 Pro is not charging beyond 80%
  • Charging Not available or Liquid has been detected in the charging port error
  • The charging dock can’t be connected to a USB-supported device through a lightning cable

If your phone has any one of these issues or something not mentioned in the list of common issues. You will still like to check out this DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may solve the problem regarding the charging dock in your iPhone 16 Pro.

  • Make sure you don’t have any debris or dirt on your charging dock. This may prevent charging
  • Make sure your power outlet isn’t faulty
  • If your phone is wet, wait until it is dry to charge your phone
  • Make sure you do not have the “optimized battery charging” option checked on your iPhone 16 Pro. if you do have it, make sure to disable it to charge your phone past 80%
  • Disable optimized Charging here: Settings > Battery > Battery Health. Note: This option is only available on iOS 13 or later updates.

The phone display doesn’t turn off during a phone call

These are the most common issues found in the iPhone 16 Pro proximity sensor. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes you may try which may solve issues regarding your proximity sensor if they are very minor. Apple recommends:

Restart your iPhone

data.title: Rear Camera Replacement
data.description:
Even with such an amazing camera, it has been found that some users have found some issues regarding the camera. The most common issues regarding the rear camera of iPhone 16 Pro found in the Apple support forum and the internet are:

  • Blurry, unclear photos
  • LED Flash is not working
  • Photos seem too noisy/ grainy
  • Camera or iPhone freezes while zooming in
  • Camera freezes/ shows a black screen after an iOS update
  • Black Display when the camera turns on/ nothing shows on the camera
  • Out of Sync flash. This is a problem where a user wants to take a photo with the flash, but the flash gets triggered after the photo has been taken

These are the most common issues that are often reported by users in Apple service centers and user forums. However, there are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available that work as a remedy for these issues. If you are facing any of the above-mentioned problems, try doing so.

  • Try Restarting your phone
  • Try cleaning your lenses with a microfiber cloth. Be careful not to scratch it
  • If your camera flash isn’t working, try turning on the flash from the control center and see if it works
  • Try disabling Voiceover settings for your iPhone. From Settings > General > Accessibility > Turn off voiceover.
  • Removing any protective cases for your phone. Especially metallic or magnetic cases, which may hamper the proper functioning of your phone’s camera
  • Try Switching between camera lenses in the settings
  • You can also try resetting your previous settings

product_data.description:
iPhone 16 Pro Original Display

This is a genuine Apple Super Retina XDR OLED display assembly for the iPhone 16 Pro, pulled from an original device — not an aftermarket or copy screen. The assembly includes the complete factory display stack: the LTPO OLED panel, the integrated touch layer, and the Ceramic Shield front glass. Every unit is function-tested before sale and comes with an 18-month warranty against display defects.

Display technology and specifications

The iPhone 16 Pro uses a 6.3-inch Super Retina XDR OLED panel with LTPO technology and a resolution of 2622×1206 pixels at 460 pixels per inch. Every specification below is the factory specification.

ProMotion adaptive refresh: The LTPO panel dynamically scales from 1Hz to 120Hz — full 120Hz smoothness for scrolling and gaming, dropping to 1Hz for the Always-On display. Aftermarket panels fixed at 60Hz cannot provide either; this one behaves exactly like the factory screen because it is one.

Brightness: 1,000 nits typical, 1,600 nits HDR peak, and 2,000 nits peak outdoor brightness with a 1-nit minimum — fully readable in direct Dhaka sunlight.

Color and calibration: Full P3 wide color with Apple's factory calibration, True Tone, and HDR including Dolby Vision.

Contrast and glass: 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio with true blacks, protected by latest-generation Ceramic Shield.

Integrated components: Factory touch digitizer with 120Hz touch sampling, Haptic Touch, ambient light sensing, and the Dynamic Island cutout at correct tolerances for the TrueDepth system.

How it compares with aftermarket and copy panels?

Aftermarket "original quality" panels for the 16 Pro typically run fixed 60Hz — losing ProMotion and Always-On, the features that define the Pro display — along with lower brightness and often lost True Tone. Copy panels drop further on every measure. The pulled original is the only grade with the complete factory specification.

Compatibility

Fits the iPhone 16 Pro only. Not compatible with the 16 Pro Max (6.9-inch), iPhone 16, 16 Plus, or 16e.

iPhone 16 Pro original display price in Bangladesh

The original iPhone 16 Pro display costs Tk 42000 at iFixit BD, including an 18-month warranty and per-unit testing before sale. The price reflects a genuine pulled Apple LTPO panel with ProMotion, Always-On, and factory brightness intact.

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water. However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage. If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • Never charge your phone until you have made sure it is completely dry

If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth. If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers. The new iPhone 16 Pro comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. This feature was made available from the iPhone X models and the later Apple A12x Bionic chipsets. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

The face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way

Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours

The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space

If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts

If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all
